proposals.note: Hierarchical entangling block with swap(0,1) symmetry. Qubits 0,1 act as global hubs (CZ to 2,3; CRZ to 4,5) capturing long-range connectivity. Qubits 2,3 and 4,5 form local pairs via CNOT. Tied RY/RX rotations per pair reduce params to 6 while preserving expressivity. The Z_2 symmetry regularizes by treating the first two nodes identically, matching the problem's node-agnostic connectivity criterion. 20 gates, 6 params — slightly deeper than c0004 but with fewer free parameters to mitigate overfitting on the 21-observable readout.

proposals.note: Ring-topology block with C6 cyclic symmetry. RZZ on ring edges directly generates Z_iZ_j correlations matching the pairwise readout observables. CRZ (parameterized) replaces CNOT for richer phase entanglement while preserving ring symmetry. Single-qubit RY and RZ add expressibility. Four tied parameters keep the model compact while the ring ensures information propagates to all 6 nodes in one block application, critical for detecting global connectivity. The C6 hypothesis encodes the natural rotational symmetry of the graph connectivity problem.

proposals.note: Two-triangle topology (0-1-2 and 3-4-5) with three cross CZ links (0,3)(1,4)(2,5) gives graph diameter 2 vs ring diameter 3, enabling faster information propagation for connectivity detection. RZZ+CRZ on both triangles create Z-basis pairwise correlations matching the 15 Z_iZ_j readout observables. Fixed CZ cross-links provide untrainable long-range entanglement that acts as a structural prior for inter-triangle connectivity. RZ on {0,1,2} only breaks the full S6 symmetry down to the (0,1,2)(3,4,5) subgroup, reducing parameter degeneracy while preserving the essential triangle-level symmetry. Four tied parameters keep the landscape smooth (low dev risk) while the mixed gate types (RZZ, CRZ, CZ, RY, RZ) span a richer expressivity than the uniform-ring c0006.

proposals.note: Builds on c0006 (best dev risk 0.3553) by replacing the ring CRZ topology with skip-1 chord CRZ gates. Ring RZZ + skip-1 CRZ together form a complete-graph entangling topology on 6 qubits, giving every pair a two-step entanglement path while preserving the cyclic (0->1->2->3->4->5) relabeling symmetry. RZZ gates directly seed Z_iZ_j correlations that the diagonal readout measures; RY/RZ provide local basis rotations to map feature-map information into the Z basis. Four tied parameters keep the block compact and reduce overfitting risk relative to c0004's seven params. The complete-graph entangling structure should better propagate connectivity information across all node pairs compared to c0006's double-ring, aiding the all-pairs reachability decision.

proposals.note: Replaced CRZ (asymmetric, control-target) in c0006 with a second RZZ layer (symmetric) on skip-2 edges. RZZ is undirected and directly produces Z_iZ_j correlations that the readout measures, matching the undirected-graph connectivity structure. Cycle RZZ (param a) captures nearest-neighbor edge info; skip-2 RZZ (param b) captures medium-range path info. RY (param c) provides the only off-diagonal mixing; RZ (param d) adds phase. Cyclic symmetry under (0 1 2 3 4 5) reduces effective parameter space and aids generalization across node labelings. 4 params, 24 gates.

proposals.note: Improvement over c0006 (dev risk 0.3553): replace distance-1 CRZ with distance-2 CRZ orbit. The 6-cycle-invariant block now entangles nearest neighbours via RZZ (p1) and applies conditional phase at next-nearest-neighbour distance via CRZ (p3), creating longer-range correlations that better detect graph disconnection. RY (p2) before CRZ ensures the conditional phase acts on superposition states, enriching the Z_iZ_j readout landscape. RZ (p4) provides final local phase tuning. Four tied parameters keep the model parsimonious while the two entangling topologies (distance-1 symmetric, distance-2 conditional) span the connectivity-relevant correlation space.

proposals.note: Multi-scale entangling block with Z6 cyclic symmetry. RY+RZ give per-qubit basis rotation; RZZ on the 6 cycle-adjacent pairs (distance-1) captures local edge correlations; CRZ on the 6 skip-one pairs (distance-2) captures path-of-length-2 correlations. Two entangling scales (d=1, d=2) let the block detect whether a spanning tree exists across all 6 nodes, directly targeting the connectivity predicate. Four tied parameters keep the parameter count low while the two-scale structure adds expressivity over single-scale designs like c0006. The Z6 invariance matches the relabeling symmetry of the connectivity question.

proposals.note: Replaced the single-ring CRZ+RZZ entanglement of c0006/c0010 with two distance-scales of RZZ (ring edges dist-1 and chord edges dist-2), both cyclically invariant. This gives the ansatz access to two independent correlation lengths within the 6-qubit ring, better matching the multi-hop connectivity structure of the graph problem. The Z_iZ_j readout at distance 1 and 2 directly probes the correlations created by rzz1 and rzz2 respectively. Cyclic shift [1,2,3,4,5,0] maps each orbit of pairs to itself, preserving invariance. 4 tied params keep gradient flow clean while 24 gates fill the budget.
